title: Calculation Techniques: Estimating, Compensating, Doubling and Halving
seo_title: Grade 6 Calculation Techniques Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use a range of techniques to perform and check written and mental calculations of whole numbers, including estimation, building up and breaking down numbers, rounding off and compensating, doubling and halving, using a number line, and using addition and subtraction as well as multiplication and division as inverse operations.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 mental maths worksheets: rounding off and compensating, doubling and halving, estimating and checking answers. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Compare every answer with an estimate.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Round off and compensate: 4 999 + 2 367 = 5 000 + 2 367 − 1.
  • Double and halve: 50 × 48 = 100 × 24 = 2 400.
  • Estimate a product by rounding both numbers: 398 × 51 is about 400 × 50 = 20 000.
  • If your answer is far from the estimate, check again.

Examples

Example

6 012 − 2 998

6 012 − 3 000 = 3 012

add back 2

Answer: 3 014

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Compensating the wrong wayYou took away too much, so add it back.
Rounding one number onlyRound both numbers.
Ignoring the estimateCompare your answer with it.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 6 say about calculation techniques?
faq.a: Use estimation, building up and breaking down numbers, rounding off and compensating, doubling and halving, a number line, and inverse operations.

faq.q: When is doubling and halving useful?
faq.a: When one number halves to an easy number, like 25 × 36 = 50 × 18.

items.q: Fatima works out 4,9 × 6,1 and gets 298,9. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 5 × 6 = 30. 298,9 is not close to 30, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 29,89; the point is in the wrong place.

items.q: Refilwe works out 7,85 + 3,4 and gets 8,19. Use an estimate to check. Is the answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 8 + 3 = 11. 8,19 is not close to 11, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 11,25. Line up the decimal points: 3,4 is 3 ones and 4 tenths, not 34 hundredths.

items.q: Pieter adds 2,4 m and 85 cm and gets 87,4 m. Is the answer reasonable?
c: Yes, the digits add up correctly
Yes, it is close to 87 m
No, it should be about 87 cm
No, it should be about 3 m
items.e: The units are different. 85 cm is less than 1 m (0,85 m). 2,4 m + 0,85 m is about 2 m + 1 m = 3 m, so 87,4 m is not reasonable. The exact answer is 3,25 m.

items.q: A bag of apples has a mass of 1,85 kg. Each apple is about 150 g. About how many apples are in the bag?
items.e: Use the same units: 1,85 kg = 1 850 g. 1 800 g ÷ 150 g = 12. (Dividing 1,85 by 150 mixes kilograms and grams.)

items.q: A recipe needs 750 mℓ of milk. Johan has a 2 ℓ bottle that is about one quarter full. Does he have enough milk?
c: No, the bottle has about 0,5 mℓ
Yes, the bottle has about 2 ℓ
No, the bottle has about 500 mℓ
Yes, the bottle has about 750 mℓ
items.e: 2 ℓ = 2 000 mℓ. One quarter of 2 000 mℓ is 500 mℓ, and 500 mℓ is less than 750 mℓ, so no.
